So suppose you were not bones but were harder than they, firmer and farther from the moisture of life; suppose you were stones whose nature is hardness and firmness; indeed suppose you were iron, the harshest kind of matter in its distance from life and its opposition to it; indeed I leave the matter to you to picture what is harder, firmer and further from accepting life, such as occurs only to the obstinate among the likes of you. For He is able to return you to life, because the One who is able to begin is able to repeat, indeed it is easier for Him, relative to our understandings and not to Him, the Exalted. This is among the wondrous and inimitable speech; indeed it is of the type that deserves not to be the speech of humans.

dervis-irab:26-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَقْعُدَ): "so you become." This is figurative. He said in al-Asās: "Figuratively: qaʿada ʿan al-amr means he left it; qaʿada lahu means he took care of it; qaʿada yashtumunī means he set about insulting me. And: he sharpened his blade until it became (qaʿadat) like a spear, that is, it became so. Al-Dayyān al-Ḥārithī said:
لأصبحن ظالما حربا رباعية ... فاقعد لها ودعن عنك الأظانينا
(I will surely make a wrongdoer a fierce warrior, a quadruped [i.e., strong] ... so set about it, and leave aside the conjectures.)
And: taqāʿada ʿan al-amr and taqaʿʿada; and mā qaʿada bihi ʿan nayl al-masāʿī, and mā tuqʿiduhu, and mā aqʿaduhu illā luʾmu ʿunṣurihi — only the baseness of his stock held him back. And he said:
بنو المجد لم تقعد بهم أمهاتهم ... وآباؤهم آباء صدق فأنجبوا
(The sons of glory — their mothers did not hold them back, and their fathers were fathers of truth, so they bore noble offspring.)"
(مَحْسُوراً): "cut off, with nothing left with you," from ḥasarahu l-safar when the journey exhausts him. In al-Mukhtār: "ḥasra is intense grief over something lost; you say ḥasira ʿalā l-shayʾ (in the pattern of ṭariba), and ḥasratan also; so he is ḥasīr; and someone else may make him grieve, taḥsīran."
(وَيَقْدِرُ): It is said qadara ʿalayhi rizqahu and qaddara, meaning "he was stingy and constricted."
(إِمْلاقٍ): "poverty and need." It is said amlaqa l-rajul: he spent his wealth until he became poor, and he is a mumliq. A Bedouin said: "May Allah fight the women! How they flatter (yatamalliqna) with pretexts, as though they draw them out from under their feet!" — that is, they bring them out.
(خِطْأً): a maṣdar of khaṭiʾa, in the pattern of ʿalima.

* I'rab:
(وَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبى حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَلا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيراً): وآت ذا القربى حقه: آت is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; ذا القربى is the direct object, and حقه is a second object; والمسكين وابن السبيل are conjoined to ذا القربى; لا is prohibitive; تبذر is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; and تبذيرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq.
(إِنَّ الْمُبَذِّرِينَ كانُوا إِخْوانَ الشَّياطِينِ): inna and its noun; the clause كانوا is its predicate; and إخوان الشياطين is the predicate of كان, meaning "their likes." The Arabs say of everyone who adheres to the practice of a people that he is their brother, for one who adheres to a thing is its brother; so they say: "so-and-so is the brother of generosity, the brother of nobility, the brother of poetry."
(وَكانَ الشَّيْطانُ لِرَبِّهِ كَفُوراً): The wāw is a conjunction or ḥāl; كان and its noun; لربه is attached to كفورا; and كفورا is the predicate of كان. It is necessary to supply an omitted muḍāf (the first term of a genitive construct), that is, "ungrateful for the favours of his Lord and His bounties."
(وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوها فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُوراً): وإما: إن is conditional and ما is redundant; تعرضن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and is in the position of jussive; its agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; عنهم is attached to تعرضن; ابتغاء رحمة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and you have two views on what governs it. Either you make it the protasis, by putting the effect in the place of the cause, that is, "and if you turn away from them because of the lack of provision from your Lord, hoping that He will open it for you," so the provision is called "mercy"; "so turn them away with a gracious refusal." Or you make it the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), which has been put before it, that is, "so say to them a generous, gentle word, and promise them a fine promise to soothe their hearts, seeking mercy from your Lord." ومن ربك is an adjective of رحمة; the clause ترجوها is a ḥāl from رحمة or a second adjective. فقل: the fāʾ is a connecting particle; قل is an imperative verb; لهم is attached to قل; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and ميسورا is an adjective.
(وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقِكَ): The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تجعل is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; يدك is the first object of تجعل and مغلولة is the second object of تجعل; and إلى عنقك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مغلولة.
(وَلا تَبْسُطْها كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُوماً مَحْسُوراً): ولا تبسطها is conjoined to لا تجعل; كل البسط is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; فتقعد: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), and تقعد is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the fāʾ preceded by a prohibition (the conditions which must precede this fāʾ will come in the section on Benefits); the agent of تقعد is latent, its implied form being "you"; and ملوما محسورا are two ḥāl, or you may make them two predicates of تقعد if you imbue it with the meaning "you become."
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ إِنَّهُ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيراً بَصِيراً): inna and its noun, and the clause يبسط is its predicate; الرزق is the direct object; لمن is attached to يبسط; the clause يشاء is the ṣila; ويقدر is conjoined to يبسط; inna and its noun, and the clause كان is the predicate of inna; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "he"; بعباده is attached to خبيرا بصيرا, and these two are the predicate of كان of inna. (وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلاقٍ): لا is prohibitive and تقتلوا is jussive by it; أولادكم is the direct object; خشية is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; and إملاق is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كانَ خِطْأً كَبِيراً): نحن is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause نرزقهم is the khabar (predicate); وإياكم is conjoined to the hāʾ; inna and its noun, and the clause كان is the predicate of inna; and خطئا is the predicate of كان, whose noun is latent, its implied form being "he"; and كبيرا is an adjective of خطئا.

* Rhetoric:
These verses comprise a group of wise sayings and proverbs and various types of rhetoric, which we summarize as follows.

1- Tamthīlī metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
In the words of Him the Exalted «ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط» there is a tamthīlī metaphor for the withholding of the miser and the giving of the spendthrift. The state of the miser, in his refusal to spend, is likened to the state of one whose hand is chained to his neck, so he is unable to handle anything; and the state of the wasteful, squandering spendthrift is likened to the state of one who stretches out his hand to the full, so that nothing is left in his palm and he keeps nothing in reserve that would benefit him in time of need — in order to arrive at a useful conclusion, namely moderation between the two extremes and thrift, which is the mean between extravagance and niggardliness. In the metaphor he made a correspondence (muṭābaqa) in meaning between the stretching out of the hand and its closing, because making the hand chained (maghlūla) is closing it, and chaining is more emphatic in closing. Abū Tammām aspired to the heaven of this meaning and said in praise of al-Muʿtaṣim:
تعود بسط الكف حتى لو أنه ... ثناها لقبض لم تطعه أنامله
(He grew so used to stretching out his palm that if he were to fold it to close it, his fingers would not obey him.)

2- Difference (al-taghāyur):
In the words of Him the Exalted «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم» — its discussion has preceded in Sūrat al-Anʿām. There is a hidden secret between what came in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ and what came in Sūrat al-Anʿām, which is His saying «ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم»; thereby he renewed a pledge. We now add to it that the killing of children, if its motive is fear of poverty, is from ill thinking of Allah and despair of His mercy; and if its motive is jealousy over girls, it is a reckless scheme from which only the destruction of society and the suspension of the landmarks of life result.

* Benefits:
The conditions for the subjunctive by an (أن) after the fāʾ of causation and the wāw of accompaniment:
An أن is not implied after the fāʾ of causation, nor after the wāw of accompaniment, except under two basic conditions, namely that they be preceded by a pure negation or a pure request (ṭalab). There is no difference in the negation whether it is a particle, a verb, a noun, or a diminution meant as negation; an example of diminution: "Seldom do you come to us so that you talk to us." As for the request, it includes seven matters, namely: the command, the prohibition, the supplication, the offer (ʿarḍ), the urging (taḥḍīḍ), the interrogative, and the wish. These seven, together with negation, become eight; some added the hope (tarajjī). One poet has gathered these nine in his saying:
مروانه وادع وسل عرض لحضّهم ... تمن وارج كذاك النفي قد كملا
(Command and forbid, and supplicate and ask, offer, urge them, wish and hope, and likewise negation — it is completed.)
We exclude by our saying "a pure negation or request": a negation followed by a question of affirmation (taqrīr) with the hamza, because taqrīr is an affirmation; a negation followed by a negation, because the negation of a negation is an affirmation; and a negation broken by illā. Among what must be observed is the saying of Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-ʿUdhrī:
ألم تسأل الربع القواء فينطق ... وهل يخبرنك اليوم بيداء سملق
(Did you not ask the empty abode, and it speaks? And will a barren desolate wasteland inform you today?)
فينطق is nominative, in the position of the nominative as a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "and it speaks"; the fāʾ is resumptive (and not causal), just as it is not a fāʾ of conjunction, since conjunction would require the jussive. Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī preferred that the fāʾ be for conjunction and that what is relied upon in the conjunction is the clause, not the verb alone; the grammarians only imply the word "he" (huwa) to make clear that the verb is not what the conjunction relies on. He said: "And similar to it is «فإنما يقول له كن فيكون», that is, 'and he is then.' And his saying:
الشعر صعب وطويل سلمه ... إذا ارتقى فيه الذي لا يعلمه
زلت به إلى الحضيض قدمه ... يريد أن يعربه فيعجمه
(Poetry is hard and its ladder long; when one who does not know it climbs it, his foot slips down with him to the bottom; he wants to make it clear and he obscures it.)
that is, 'and he obscures it.'"
Let us return to the verse of Jamīl and say: Sībawayh cited it in his book and said, verbatim: "He did not make the first the cause of the second, but made it speak in any case, as if he had said, 'and it is among things that speak,' just as one says 'Come to me and I will tell you,' making himself one who tells him in any case. Yūnus claimed that he heard this verse; I only wrote that so that no one would say: perhaps the poet said it differently (إلا) — end." Ibn al-Naḥḥās said: "Its meaning is taqrīr — that you asked it, so the subjunctive is ugly, because the meaning would be that if you ask it, it speaks." Al-Aʿlam said: "The point of citation is the nominative of ينطق as resumptive and as a break, in the sense of 'so it speaks,' and the affirmation of that; and if the subjunctive were possible as an answer, it would have been better."
Al-Farrāʾ said: "That is: 'you have asked it and it spoke.' If you made it an interrogative and made the fāʾ conditional, you would put it in the subjunctive, as another said:
ألم تسأل فتخبرك الديارا ... عن الحي المضلّل حيث سارا
(Did you not ask, that the abodes might inform you about the misguided tribe, where it travelled?)
And the jussive in this verse is permissible, as he said:
فقلت له صوب ولا تجهدنه ... فيدرك من أخرى القطاة فتزلق
(I said to him, 'Go down, and do not strain him' — then he overtakes the last of the sandgrouse and slips.)
so he made the answer with the fāʾ as if conjoined to what precedes."
Given the importance of this verse and the scholars' attention to it, we say that it is the opening of a poem by Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-ʿUdhrī, the famous companion of Buthayna, and after it, from fine poetry:
بمختلف الأرواح بين سويقة ... وأحدب كادت بعد عهدك تخلق
أضرت بها النكباء كل عشية ... ونفح الصبا والوابل المتعبق
وقفت بها حتى تجلت عمايتي ... ومل الوقوف الأرحبيّ المنوّق
وقال صديقي: إن ذا لصبابة ... ألا تزجر القلب اللجوج فيلحق؟
تعزّ وإن كانت عليك كريمة ... لعلك من أسباب بثنة تعتق
فقلت له: إن البعاد يشوقني ... وبعض بعاد البين والنأي أشوق
(At the meeting-place of the winds between Suwayqa and Aḥdab, it almost wore away after your time; the north wind harmed it every evening, as did the puffs of the east wind and the perfumed downpour. I stood there until my blindness cleared, and the Arḥabī camel, tamed, grew tired of standing. My friend said: "This is a passion — will you not rein in the stubborn heart so that it follows?" "Console yourself, though she is dear to you; perhaps you will be freed from the ties of Buthayna." I said to him: "Distance only makes me yearn, and some of the distance of separation and remoteness yearns more.")
Al-rabʿ is the dwelling; al-qawāʾ is the wasteland. He made it speak in order to draw a lesson from its effacement and change, then he affirmed and reported that it does not answer or inform its questioner, because there are no inhabitants in it. Al-baydāʾ is the wasteland; al-samlaq is the land in which there is nothing.
Among what was disputed and was a place of subtlety is the saying of ʿUrwa al-ʿUdhrī, the companion of ʿAfrāʾ:
وما هو إلا أن أراها فجاءة ... فأبهت حتى ما أكاد أجيب
(It is nothing but that I see her suddenly, and I am struck dumb until I can scarcely answer.)
Sībawayh said: "I asked al-Khalīl about the poet's saying: 'وما هو إلا أن أراها…', and he said: 'You have a choice with فأبهت: if you wish you may carry it on أن, and if you wish you may not carry it on it, and put it in the nominative, as though you said: It is nothing but the sight, and I am struck dumb.'" What Sībawayh meant is that the subjunctive is by conjunction, since what is meant is the maṣdar, the estimate being "It is nothing but the seeing, and then my being struck dumb"; and the nominative is by break and resumption, the meaning being "and then I am stupefied." We have dwelt on this because it is a matter of subtlety, so understand it and measure by it.

dervis-irab:82-84.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَأى): "Turning aside with one's side" means that he turns his flank and turns his back; what is meant is arrogance, because that is the habit of the arrogant. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "naʾā, naʾyan, of the pattern of nafaʿa [«من باب نفع»], means he went far away." It takes its object directly or through a preposition, the latter being more frequent, so one says naʾaytuhu and naʾaytu ʿanhu; and it is made transitive by the hamza, so one says anʾaytuhu.
(شاكِلَتِهِ): His way and his path, which matches his state in guidance and error, from their saying "a road with shawākil", meaning the roads that branch off from it. The meaning is: every person acts according to the essence of his soul. If his soul is noble and pure, beautiful deeds proceed from him; and if his soul is turbid and vile, vile and corrupt deeds proceed from him.

* I'rab:
(وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ما هُوَ شِفاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ننزل) is an imperfect verb, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we". (ومن القرآن) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the view that (من) is explicative; it may also be for the beginning of the range or partitive, in which case it is attached to (ننزل), as Abū Ḥayyān preferred. (ما) is a direct object; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (شفاء) its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (رحمة) is conjoined to (شفاء), and (للمؤمنين) is attached to (شفاء).
(وَلا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا خَساراً) The wāw is circumstantial; (لا) is negative; (يزيد الظالمين) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (خسارا) is a second direct object.
(وَإِذا أَنْعَمْنا عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأى بِجانِبِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction and (إذا) is an adverb of the future. The clause (أنعمنا) is annexed to the adverb; it consists of a verb and an agent, and (على الإنسان) is attached to it. The clause (أعرض) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (نأى) is conjoined to (أعرض), and (بجانبه) is attached to (نأى).
(وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ كانَ يَؤُساً) Conjoined to what precedes. The clause (مسه الشر) is annexed to the adverb, and the clause (كان) has no grammatical position. The name of (كان) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", and (يئوسا) is the khabar of (كان).
(قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلى شاكِلَتِهِ) (كل) is a mubtadaʾ, meaning "every one"; the clause (يعمل) is the khabar, and (على شاكلته) is attached to (يعمل).
(فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدى سَبِيلًا) The fāʾ is resumptive; (ربكم) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعلم) its khabar; (بمن) is attached to (أعلم); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أهدى) its khabar, the clause being a ṣila; and (سبيلا) is a tamyīz (specification).

dervis-irab:85-87.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ) The wāw is resumptive. (يسألونك) is an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object, and (عن الروح) is attached to (يسألونك). The pronoun refers to the obstinate Jews, who asked him, out of malice, about the Companions of the Cave, about Dhū l-Qarnayn and about the Spirit; so he explained the two stories to them but left the matter of the Spirit vague, and it is left vague in the Torah.
(قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَما أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) (الروح) is a mubtadaʾ and (من أمر ربي) its khabar, meaning that it is among the things whose knowledge Allah has reserved to Himself. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (ما) is negative; (أوتيتم) is a passive past verb; (من العلم) is attached to (أوتيتم); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (قليلا) is the second direct object of (أوتيتم), that is, "a little thing" in relation to His knowledge, the Exalted, even if it is much in itself.
(وَلَئِنْ شِئْنا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the one that prepares for an oath; (إن) is conditional; (شئنا) is a past verb and an agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The lām of (لنذهبن) is the apodosis of the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, that is "we would take it away", following the rule that when a condition and an oath come together, the apodosis of the later one is omitted, being dispensed with by the apodosis of the earlier one. (بالذي) is attached to (لنذهبن); the clause (أوحينا) is a ṣila; and (إليك) is attached to (أوحينا).
(ثُمَّ لا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِ عَلَيْنا وَكِيلًا) (ثم) is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (تجد) is an imperfect nominative verb whose agent is "you"; (لك) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (وكيلا); (به) is attached to (تجد); (علينا) is attached to (وكيلا); and (وكيلا) is a direct object, meaning: you will not find anyone who would act as an agent on our behalf to recover it after it was taken away.
(إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّ فَضْلَهُ كانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيراً) It is permissible for this exception to be connected (muttaṣil), because the Spirit is included under (وكيلا), that is "except mercy", in which case it is the excepted, or a badal (substitute) for (وكيلا). It is also permissible for it to be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), with (إلا) meaning "but", and then (رحمة) is parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the implied meaning being "we preserved it for you out of mercy", or as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied meaning being "but we showed you mercy". (من ربك) is an adjective of (رحمة). (إن) and its name, and the clause (كان) is its khabar; (عليك) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (كبيرا); and (كبيرا) is the khabar of (كان).

dervis-irab:88-89.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هذَا الْقُرْآنِ) (لئن): the lām prepares for an oath, and (إن) is conditional. (اجتمعت) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis. (الإنس) is the agent, and (الجن) is conjoined to (الإنس). As for (على أن يأتوا): (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of the genitive after (على), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, meaning "supporting one another and cooperating". (بمثل) is attached to (يأتوا); (هذا) is annexed to (مثل); and (القرآن) is a badal.
(لا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ وَلَوْ كانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيراً) (لا يأتون): (لا) is negative, and (يأتون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative because it is the apodosis of the omitted oath, which came first, and not the apodosis of the condition. The wāw is the agent, and (بمثله) is attached to (يأتون). As for (ولو): the wāw is circumstantial and (لو) is the connective (waṣliyya). (كان) is a defective past verb; (بعضهم) is the name of (كان); (لبعض) is attached to (ظهيرا); and (ظهيرا) is the khabar of (كان). The clause (لو كان …) is a ḥāl. For this construction there is a rule, which we shall give in the section on Benefits.
(وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for an oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation; (صرفنا) is a verb and an agent; (في هذا) is attached to (صرفنا); (القرآن) is a badal; and (من كل مثل) is an adjective of the omitted direct object, that is "of every meaning that is like a parable in its rarity and beauty".
(فَأَبى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُوراً) (فأبى) is conjoined to (صرفنا); (أكثر الناس) is the agent; and (إلا) is a particle of restriction, because (أبى) is interpreted as a negation, as if it had been said: "they were not satisfied with anything but disbelief". (كفورا) is a direct object.

* Benefits:
When a conjunction comes before the connective (لو), it is conjoined to something implied, and omitting the thing conjoined to is regular, since the conjoined element points to it unmistakably. So in His saying, the Exalted, «ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا», the conjunction here is to something implied, that is: "they would not produce the like of it if they were not supporters of one another, and even if they were supporters of one another." For if producing the like of it is ruled out when they support one another, then it is all the more ruled out when they do not. On this subtle point turns the emphasis found in the two connective forms (إن) and (لو). Its position is the accusative as a ḥāl, in accordance with what is conjoined to it, that is: "they will not produce the like of it under any supposed circumstance, even in this circumstance, which runs contrary to their not producing it, let alone any other."

dervis-irab:53-57.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is joined to what preceded so as to complete the teachings by which their affairs are upheld. قل: imperative verb, the agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". لعبادي: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قل. يقولوا is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), or it is jussive by the omitted lām of command; the details of this construction were given in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, so renew your acquaintance with it there. التي is the direct object of يقولوا or, more correctly, an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "the word that is best". هي is the mubtadaʾ and أحسن the khabar, and the clause is a ṣila. (إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ يَنْزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ كانَ لِلْإِنْسانِ عَدُوًّا مُبِيناً) The clause gives a reason for His words يقولوا التي هي أحسن. إن and its noun; the clause ينزغ بينهم, i.e. "he sows corruption among them", is the khabar. The second clause إن الشيطان is a badal of the first. كان: incomplete past verb. للانسان: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عدوا. عدوا is the khabar of kāna, and مبينا is an adjective of عدوا. The clause كان etc. is the khabar of inna. (رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِنْ يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ) ربكم is the mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; بكم: attached to أعلم. إن is conditional; يشأ is the protasis, jussive; يرحمكم is the apodosis, also jussive. (أَوْ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًا) It is conjoined to what preceded. The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative. أرسلناك: verb and agent. عليهم: attached to وكيلا. وكيلا is a ḥāl from the kāf, i.e. "one to whom their affair is entrusted, so that you strive for their guidance". (وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) وربك is the mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; بمن: attached to أعلم; and في السموات والأرض is a ṣila. (وَلَقَدْ فَضَّلْنا بَعْضَ النَّبِيِّينَ عَلى بَعْضٍ وَآتَيْنا داوُدَ زَبُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the one that prepares for an oath; قد is a particle of affirmation. فضلنا: verb and agent. بعض النبيين: direct object. على بعض: attached to فضلنا. آتينا is conjoined to فضلنا; it is a verb and agent. داود is the first direct object and زبورا the second direct object. The secret of singling out Dāwūd with the giving of the Zabūr will come in the section on benefits.
(قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ) The clause ادعوا الذين is the content of what is said. ادعوا: imperative verb and agent. الذين: direct object. The clause زعمتم is a ṣila; the two objects of زعمتم are omitted because they are known, and they are "you claimed them to be gods". من دونه: the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, accusative as a ḥāl. (فَلا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنْكُمْ وَلا تَحْوِيلًا) The fāʾ is resumptive, and لا is negative. يملكون كشف الضر: imperfect verb, agent and direct object. عنكم: attached to كشف. The wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and تحويلا is conjoined to كشف الضر. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلى رَبِّهِمُ الْوَسِيلَةَ)
أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين يدعون is a badal of it; the clause يبتغون is the khabar, the wāw being the agent; إلى ربهم: attached to الوسيلة; and الوسيلة is the direct object. It is permissible for you to parse الذين as the khabar, and the clause يبتغون as a ḥāl from the agent of يدعون. (أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُ وَيَخافُونَ عَذابَهُ) أيهم is a badal of the agent of يبتغون, and أي is a relative; it may also be interrogative, being then a mubtadaʾ with أقرب as khabar. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān [Translator's note: the text reads «أبي حياة», evidently a misprint for أبي حيان]: «They differed on the parsing of أيهم أقرب and its implied form. Al-Ḥawfī said: أيهم أقرب is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the meaning is "they look to see which of them is nearest, so that they may seek nearness through him"; and it is permissible that أيهم أقرب be a badal of the wāw in يبتغون.» In the first view a suspending verb (fiʿl al-taʿlīq) is implied, and أيهم أقرب is in the position of the accusative on the dropping of the preposition, because نظر, if it means reflecting, is made transitive by في, and if it is seeing with the eye, it is made transitive by إلى; so the clause from which the verb is suspended, on either assumption, is in the position of the accusative on the dropping of the preposition, as in His words «فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما»; and the implied suspending verb is نظر. The second view was stated by al-Zamakhsharī, who said: «أي may be relative, i.e. "he seeks, whoever is nearest of them and closest, the means to Allah; so what of one who is not the nearest?"» According to this view أقرب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and it is possible that أيهم is declinable (muʿrab), which is the preferred view, and possible that it is indeclinable (mabnī) because of the presence of a justification for indeclinability; the rule on «أي» will come in the section on benefits. أقرب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the meaning is "they seek, whoever is nearest of them and has approached them by the nearness of the means to Allah; so what of one who is not the nearest? How then do they claim that they are gods?" يرجون رحمته is conjoined to يبتغون. يرجون: imperfect verb and agent; the lām of the verb, which is the wāw, was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. رحمته: direct object. ويخافون عذابه is conjoined to يرجون رحمته. (إِنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّكَ كانَ مَحْذُوراً) This is a reason for the fear. إن and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "it"; and محذورا is the khabar of كان.

* Benefits:
1- The meaning of preferring some prophets over others:
The preferring of some prophets over others is by the difference in qualities of the soul, and for this reason the Ulū al-ʿAzm (those of firm resolve) among them became famous, those targeted for trial who neither weakened nor yielded; and Muḥammad ﷺ was the seal of the prophets, marked with the complete attributes. The singling out of Dāwūd with the Zabūr contains a rebuttal of the Jews who claimed that there is no prophet after Mūsā and no book after the Torah. The word الزبور has been used with the definite article and without it, with an eye to the origin, because it is of the pattern فعول with the sense of the passive, like الحلوب meaning المحلوبة (the milked), or because He meant a portion of the Zabūr.

2- أي:
It comes in six ways:
1- Conditional: «أيّا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى», by the evidence of the jussive تدعوا and the entry of the fāʾ as a link to the nominal clause; and أيّا ما is the direct object of تدعوا.
2- Interrogative: «أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا», «فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون».
3- Relative: «لننزعنّ من كل شيعة أيهم أشد»; the implied form is "We shall surely draw out the one who is most intense".
4- Indicating perfection, so that it occurs as an adjective of an indefinite, as in زيد رجل أيّ رجل ("Zayd is a man, what a man"), and as a ḥāl of a definite, as in مررت بعبد الله أيّ رجل ("I passed by ʿAbd Allāh, what a man").
5- Being a means to vocative address of what has the article al-, as in يا أيها الرجل; its indeclinability on the ḍamma is obligatory only so that it be in the form of the single vocative that is intended by the call, since it ends in ḍamma.
6- Being for exclamation, as in سبحان الله أيّ رجل هذا ("Glory be to Allah, what a man this is").
And أيّ is declinable (muʿrab) in all its states, except when it is a relative, annexed, and the beginning of its ṣila is omitted as mentioned above, in which case it is indeclinable on the ḍamma. For أيّ there are details to which the longer works should be consulted, and further discussion of it will come.

dervis-irab:9-15.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ) إن and its noun; القرآن is a badal of the demonstrative. يهدي is a verb with a latent agent, and the direct object is omitted, that is, "he guides the people"; the clause is the khabar of إن. وللتي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يهدي. هي is a mubtadaʾ and أقوم its khabar, and the nominal clause is the ṣila of التي. أقوم is a comparative noun (ism tafḍīl) according to al-Zajjāj, since he implied "the most upright of states"; others implied "more upright than what is other than them" or "than every state". Abū Ḥayyān preferred that it is not comparative, saying: there is no sharing between the way to which the Qur'an guides and the way of others, so that this one is preferred over them; rather, the meaning is "the one that is qayyima", that is, straight, as He said: "and that is the religion of the qayyima" and "in them are qayyima scriptures", that is, of straight way, standing by what is needed of the matter of religion.
(وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً كَبِيراً) ويبشر is conjoined to يهدي, and المؤمنين is a direct object. الذين is an adjective of المؤمنين, and the clause يعملون is the ṣila; الصالحات is a direct object. أن and what is in its scope are accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to يبشر. لهم is the fronted khabar of أن, and أجرا is its postponed noun, and كبيرا an adjective.
(وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنا لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) وأن الذين is conjoined to "أن لهم أجرا كبيرا", that is, He gives the believers two great glad tidings: the first of their reward and the second of the punishment of their enemies. It is also permissible for it to be conjoined to يبشر with an implied "and He informs that those who do not believe are to be punished". The clause أعتدنا is the khabar of أن, and لهم is attached to أعتدنا; عذابا is a direct object and أليما an adjective.
(وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ عَجُولًا) The wāw is resumptive; ويدعو الإنسان is a verb and agent. بالشر is attached to an omitted ḥāl or to يدعو, and دعاءه is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. بالخير is also a ḥāl, or is attached to الدعاء, because it is a maṣdar. The wāw is a conjunction or a circumstantial one (ḥāliyya); كان with its noun and khabar.
(وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ آيَتَيْنِ فَمَحَوْنا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ) وجعلنا is a verb and agent, الليل a direct object, النهار conjoined to الليل, and آيتين a second direct object. فمحونا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and محونا is conjoined to جعلنا; آية الليل is a direct object.
(وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) وجعلنا is a verb and agent, آية النهار the first direct object and مبصرة the second direct object. ولتبتغوا: the lām is for causation, and تبتغوا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation; the wāw is the agent, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to His saying وجعلنا. فضلا is a direct object, and من ربكم is attached to تبتغوا and is an adjective of His word فضلا.
(وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسابَ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلًا) ولتعلموا is conjoined to ولتبتغوا; عدد السنين is a direct object, and الحساب is conjoined to عدد, and there is no redundancy in the two. كل شيء is accusative by ishtighāl (the preoccupied noun), and its accusative is preferred because of the preceding verbal clause, as will come in the Benefits section. فصلناه is a verb, agent and direct object, and تفصيلا a mafʿūl muṭlaq.
(وَكُلَّ إِنسانٍ أَلْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ) وكل إنسان is also accusative by ishtighāl. ألزمناه is a verb, agent and direct object, and طائره a second direct object, and في عنقه a ḥāl, that is, "being"; the detail of that will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ كِتاباً يَلْقاهُ مَنْشُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction, and نخرج is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we". له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نخرج, and كتابا is a direct object. The clause يلقاه is an adjective of كتابا, and منشورا is either a second adjective of كتابا or a ḥāl.
(اقْرَأْ كِتابَكَ كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيباً) The clause اقرأ كتابك is in the position of the accusative, being the quoted speech of an omitted "saying", that is, "it is said to him". اقرأ is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and كتابك is a direct object. كفى is a past verb, and بنفسك: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and نفسك is the agent, nominative in position and genitive in form by the bāʾ. اليوم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, and عليك is attached to حسيبا. حسيبا is a tamyīz, in the sense of ḥāsib (one who reckons), as Sībawayh mentioned. Sībawayh said: "ḍarīb al-qidāḥ is in the sense of ḍāribuhā, and ṣarīm in the sense of ṣārim." Some permitted its analysis as a ḥāl because it is derived, and that is not far-fetched.
(مَنِ اهْتَدى فَإِنَّما يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ) من is conditional and a mubtadaʾ, and اهتدى is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis. فإنما: the fāʾ is the connector, and إنما is "kāffa" and "makfūfa" [the restraining particle together with the restrained]; يهتدي is an imperfect verb, nominative, with the agent "huwa" (he); لنفسه is attached to يهتدي, and the clause accompanied by the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّما يَضِلُّ عَلَيْها) This is conjoined to the preceding sentence. عليها is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "its straying falling upon it".
(وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى) The wāw is a conjunction and لا negative; تزر is an imperfect verb and agent, and وزر is the object of تزر, that is, "bears"; أخرى is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(وَما كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا) The wāw is a conjunction and ما negative; كنا is kāna and its noun, and معذبين its khabar. حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive case; نبعث is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after حتى, and رسولا is a direct object.

* Rhetoric:
1- Mental trope (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī) in His saying "and We made the sign of the day sight-giving (mubṣira)", because the day does not see; rather, one sees in it. So it is an ascription of the action to its time, and it has often been mentioned before.
2- «وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه»: an expression conveyed according to the custom of the Arabs. They would not undertake any important work without considering the states of the birds, to see whether the outcome of the work would be good or evil. If the birds flew of themselves or by someone's startling them toward the right, they took it as a good omen and set about their work; and if they flew toward the left, they took it as an ill omen and held back from their work. As this became frequent among them, they called good and evil themselves "the bird", naming a thing by the name of its concomitant, by way of the unrestricted trope (majāz mursal), which has often been mentioned before.
He singled out the neck for mention only because it is the place of the necklace that adorns the neck, appears at first glance, and marks the one who wears it with beauty. So that was a metonymy (kināya) for his being characterised by the good and evil decreed for him in the Tablet of eternity, and for his preferring, by his own choice, one side of them, like the one who follows the sawāniḥ, which are birds going toward the right, and the one who follows the bawāriḥ, which are birds going toward the left. Some permitted that the speech be of the category of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), that is, "the bird" is borrowed for what is the cause of good and evil, from Allah's decree and the servant's action; that is, since they made the bird a cause of good and evil and ascribed both to it on account of its going right or left, "the bird" was borrowed for what is a cause of them, namely Allah's existing power and the chosen action of the servant. And just as the real bird comes to every place after leaving its nests, so events reach the human being.
3- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between guidance and misguidance, which has already been discussed.
4- In His saying "And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day sight-giving" there is the art of combination with differentiation (al-jamʿ maʿa l-tafrīq), which is that the speaker combines two things under one ruling, then differentiates between them in that ruling. Among its occurrences in poetry is the wonderful saying of al-Buḥturī:
ولما التقينا والنقا موعد لنا ... تعجب رائي الدرّ منّا ولا قطه
فمن لؤلؤ تجلوه عند ابتسامها ... ومن لؤلؤ عند الحديث تساقطه
(When we met, with the dune as our tryst, the one who saw the pearls marvelled at us, and the one who gathered them: from pearls she displays when she smiles, and from pearls that drop when she speaks.)

* Benefits:
Ishtighāl (preoccupation):
The grammarians defined ishtighāl as a noun that precedes a governor which by right would make it accusative, were it not for the governor's being occupied with acting upon the pronoun of the noun, as in: "Khālid, I honoured him." The better case for the fronted noun is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the clause after it as its khabar; and it may be accusative by an omitted verb which the verb mentioned after it explains. The clause "ra'aytuhu" is explicative of the implied clause and has no grammatical position, and it is not permissible to show the implied verb; it is implied with the wording of the mentioned verb, unless it is intransitive, in which case it is implied by its meaning, as in "Ḥimṣ, I passed by it", where it is implied, for example, as "I crossed". It has several states:

1- The accusative is obligatory:
That is when it occurs after particles of urging, condition and interrogation other than the hamza, as in "Hallā l-khayr faʿaltuhu" (Why did you not do the good?), "Inna ʿAliyyan laqītuhu fa-sallim ʿalayhi" (If you meet ʿAlī, greet him), and "Hal Khālidan akramtahu?" (Did you honour Khālid?). However, ishtighāl after particles of interrogation and condition occurs only in poetry.

2- The accusative is preferred:
The accusative is preferred in five matters:
(a) That a command follow the noun, as in "Khālidan akrimhu" (Honour Khālid). Excepted from that is the case of "As for the thief, male and female, cut off their hands", which has already been discussed fully.
(b) That a prohibition follow the noun, as in "al-karīm lā tuhinhu" (Do not humiliate the noble man).
(c) That a supplication follow the noun, as in "Allāhumma amrī yassirhu" (O Allah, make my affair easy).
(d) That the noun occur after the interrogative hamza, as in His saying "Shall we follow a single man from among us?"
(e) That the noun be an answer to something asked about, as you say "ʿAliyyan akramtuhu" in answer to one who says "Whom did you honour?"

3- The nominative is obligatory:
The nominative is obligatory in two places:
1- That it occur after the sudden "idhā", as in "I went out, and suddenly the air was filled with fog", because the sudden idhā does not enter verbs.
2- That it occur before particles of interrogation, condition, urging, negative mā, the lām of commencement, the mā of exclamation, the khabariyya kam, or inna and its sisters, as in: "ʿAlī, did you honour him?", "Saʿīd, if you meet him, greet him", "Khālid, why did you not call him?", "the evil, I did not do it", "the good, I do it", "good character, how good it is!", "Zuhayr, how many times I have honoured him", "Khālid, I love him". In all of these the noun is a mubtadaʾ and the clause after it is the khabar. Its accusative is not permitted only because these particles have the right to the beginning of the sentence, and what follows them does not govern what precedes them.

4- The nominative is preferred:
The nominative is preferred when there is nothing that makes the accusative obligatory or preferred or makes the nominative obligatory, as in "al-kitāb qara'tuhu" (The book, I read it), because non-implication is better than implication.
There are matters related to ishtighāl that can be consulted in the longer works, and interesting subtleties of it will come in this book.

dervis-irab:94-96.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما مَنَعَ النَّاسَ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إِذْ جاءَهُمُ الْهُدى) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (ما) is negative; (منع) is a past verb; (الناس) is a fronted direct object; (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of (منع); (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (منع), that is: "nothing prevented people from belief at the time guidance came to them". The clause (جاءهم الهدى) is the one annexed to the adverb.
(إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا: أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَراً رَسُولًا) (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of the nominative as the agent of (منع). The hamza is for a rhetorical question of denial, and what they denied is the thing denounced. (بعث الله) is a verb and an agent; (بشرا) is a ḥāl from (رسولا), because it was originally an adjective of it and was put before it, as is the rule; and (رسولا) is a direct object.
(قُلْ لَوْ كانَ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَلائِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ) (قل) is an imperative verb; (لو) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb; (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted khabar of (كان), which is put first; (ملائكة) is its postponed name; the clause (يمشون) is an adjective of (ملائكة); and (مطمئنين) is a ḥāl. It is also permissible for (كان) to be complete (tāmma), with (ملائكة) as its agent.
(لَنَزَّلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ مَلَكاً رَسُولًا) The lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو). (نزلنا) is a verb and an agent; (عليهم) is attached to (نزلنا); (من السماء) is also attached to (نزلنا); (ملكا) is a ḥāl from (رسولا); and (رسولا) is the object of (نزلنا).
(قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ) (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (الله) is genitive by the bāʾ in form and is the agent of (كفى) in position; (شهيدا) is a tamyīz (specification); the adverb (بيني) is attached to (شهيدا); and (بينكم) is conjoined to the first adverb.
(إِنَّهُ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيراً بَصِيراً) (إن) and its name; the clause (كان) is its khabar; and (خبيرا بصيرا) are two khabars of (كان).

dervis-irab:97-100.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ) The wāw is resumptive. (من) is a conditional noun that jusses, in the position of the accusative, a fronted object of (يهد). (يهد) is the protasis and (الله) the agent. (فهو): the fāʾ links the apodosis, because it is a nominal clause; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (المهتدي) its khabar, the yāʾ being dropped in the Qur'anic orthography. The clause (هو المهتدي) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من), according to the sounder view.
(وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the one before it. (لهم) is attached to (أولياء), and (من دونه) is a ḥāl.
(وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْياً وَبُكْماً وَصُمًّا) (ونحشرهم): the wāw is resumptive; (نحشرهم) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. (يوم القيامة) is attached to (نحشرهم). (على وجوههم) is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (نحشرهم). (عميا) and what is conjoined to it are likewise ḥāls.
(مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ كُلَّما خَبَتْ زِدْناهُمْ سَعِيراً) (مأواهم جهنم) is a resumptive clause composed of a mubtadaʾ and a khabar. (كلما) is an adverb containing the meaning of a condition, as has already been given; it is attached to the apodosis, which is (زدناهم). (سعيرا) is a second direct object. The clause (كلما خبت) is a ḥāl from (جهنم).
(ذلِكَ جَزاؤُهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا) (ذلك) is a demonstrative and a mubtadaʾ; (جزاؤهم) is its khabar; (بأنهم): (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جزاؤهم). It is also permissible for (جزاؤهم) to be a badal of (ذلك) and for (بأنهم) to be the khabar. The clause (كفروا) is the khabar of (أن), and (بآياتنا) is attached to (كفروا).
(وَقالُوا أَإِذا كُنَّا عِظاماً وَرُفاتاً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقاً جَدِيداً) The hamza is for a rhetorical question of denial. (إذا) is an adverb of the future. (كنا عظاما): (كان), its name and its khabar; (رفاتا) is conjoined to (عظاما). The hamza is again for a rhetorical question of denial. (إن) and its name; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (مبعوثون) is the khabar of (إنا); (خلقا) is a ḥāl and (جديدا) an adjective. You may also make (خلقا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) derived from the meaning of the verb, that is: "we shall be raised with a new raising".
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ قادِرٌ عَلى أَنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ) The hamza is for a rhetorical question of denial, in reply to their denial. The wāw is a conjunction to something omitted, a point already established many times. (أن) and what is within its scope take the place of the two objects of (يروا). (الذي) is an adjective of (الله); the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is a ṣila; (قادر) is the khabar of (أن); (على أن) is attached to (قادر); and (مثلهم) is an adjective of the omitted direct object, that is "a creation like them". The explanation of this is that the like of a thing is its equal in some respect, so it is permissible to express the thing itself by it.
(وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَجَلًا لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) The wāw is a conjunction. (جعل) is conjoined to «أو لم يروا», because it is in the sense of "they have seen"; the meaning is: "they have come to know by the evidence of reason that He who is able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create their like, and that a term has been appointed for them." (لهم) is attached to an omitted second object of (جعل), and (أجلا) is the first object of (جعل). The clause (لا ريب فيه) is an adjective of (أجلا): (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ريب) is its name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and (فيه) is its khabar.
(فَأَبَى الظَّالِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُوراً) Its explanation was given a little earlier, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(قُلْ لَوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي) (لو) is conditional, and it properly enters upon verbs rather than nouns, so a verb must be implied which what follows explains, that is "if you possessed". When it was implied on condition of being explained, the pronoun became detached, so (أنتم) is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the latent agent in the omitted verb that what follows explains. The discussion of this will come in detail in the section on Benefits.
Whoever parsed (أنتم) as an agent made a mistake, because the pronoun of the addressee may not be made overt. The clause (تملكون) is explicative, with no grammatical position, and (خزائن رحمة ربي) is a direct object.
(إِذاً لَأَمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ الْإِنْفاقِ وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ قَتُوراً) (إذن) is a particle of answer and consequence, not operative. In (لأمسكتم) the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو), and the clause has no grammatical position. (خشية الإنفاق) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The wāw is circumstantial; (كان الإنسان قتورا): (كان), its name and its khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. The explanation of this meaning will come in the section on Benefits.

* Benefits:
1- (لو) and the noun after it:
It has been said in more than one place in this book that a condition can only be with verbs, because you make the existence of something else depend on the existence of the verb, whereas nouns are fixed and existent, and it is not sound to make the existence of anything depend on their existence. For that reason only a verb follows the particle of condition, and it is ugly for the noun to precede the verb in it. (لو) falls within this definition, and when a noun comes after it and a verb after the noun, the noun is governed by an omitted verb before it, which the overt verb explains. That is because it requires a verb rather than a noun. Among the sayings of Ḥātim: «لو ذات سوار لطمتني» ("had a woman wearing a bracelet slapped me"), on the implied form "had a woman wearing a bracelet slapped me".
2- The meaning of «وكان الإنسان قتورا»:
One of the obstinate raised an objection against His saying, the Exalted, «وكان الإنسان قتورا», and said, in the manner of obstinacy and verbal disputation: How can this universal negation be sound? How can the whole human genus be tight-fisted and miserly when we see among the children of Adam the generous and noble? The answer is extremely simple: the constitution of man is in origin founded on need, and on being stingy with what he needs in order to keep that on which his livelihood and the foundation of his affairs rest; and the winning of a good name and fragrant praise is the goal of what he spends, so much so that among them there is, as the objector said, not only the generous and noble but one who regards giving of himself and his dearest possessions as right, in the words of the poet:
يجود بالنفس إن ضن الجواد بها ... والجود بالنفس أقصى غاية الجود
(He gives of his very self if the generous man is stingy with it; and giving of oneself is the utmost limit of generosity.)
3- Some of the later grammarians held that the adverbial (إذا) is to be measured against (إذ) in having tanwīn attached to it: when the clause to which it is annexed is omitted, tanwīn is given in exchange for it, as in His saying, the Exalted, «وإذا لآتيناهم», «وإذا لأمسكتم», «وإذا لأذقناك», «وإذا لا يلبثون» and «إنكم إذا لمن المقربين». They said that (إذا) in these examples is not the one that puts the imperfect in the accusative, because that one is specific to it and therefore operates upon it, and only what is specific operates, whereas this one is not specific to it but enters upon the past verb and upon the noun. Among those who mentioned this are al-Kāfiyajī, Abū Ḥayyān in his Tadhkira and al-Zarkashī in al-Burhān, and we do not think it far-fetched. They said: "You say to one who said 'I shall come to you': إذًا أكرمك (then I shall honour you)", with the imperfect in the nominative, in the sense of "if you come to me, I shall honour you"; so "you come to me" is omitted, tanwīn is given in exchange for the clause, and the alif drops because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

dervis-irab:58-60.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوها قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوها عَذاباً شَدِيداً) The wāw is resumptive, and إن is negative. من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and قرية is genitive in form and nominative in position, as mubtadaʾ. إلا is a particle of restriction. نحن is a mubtadaʾ and مهلكوها its khabar, and the nominal clause is the khabar of قرية. قبل يوم القيامة: the adverbial, attached to مهلكوها. أو is a conjunction, and معذبوها is conjoined to مهلكوها. عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and شديدا is a ṣila [Translator's note: so the text reads; the evident intent is that شديدا is an adjective of عذابا]. (كانَ ذلِكَ فِي الْكِتابِ مَسْطُوراً) كان and its noun; وفي الكتاب: attached to مسطورا; and مسطورا is the khabar of kāna. (وَما مَنَعَنا أَنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالْآياتِ إِلَّا أَنْ كَذَّبَ بِهَا الْأَوَّلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative. منعنا: past verb with a fronted direct object. أن نرسل: the interpreted maṣdar is the second object of منع. بالآيات: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, on the pattern of its redundancy in the words of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
وقد علم القبائل من معد ... إذا قبب بأبطحها بنينا
بأنا المطعمون إذا أردنا ... وأنا النازلون بحيث شينا
(The tribes of Maʿadd know, when we pitch tents in their valley, that we are the ones who feed when we wish, and that we alight wherever we please.)
You may also make it original, in which case it is for accompaniment (mulābasa) and the object is omitted, i.e. in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and the meaning is "and nothing prevented Us from sending a prophet while he is accompanied by the signs". إلا is a particle of restriction. The second أن and what is in its scope are in the position of the nominative as the agent of منع. بها: attached to كذب, and الأولون is the agent. (وَآتَيْنا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا بِها) This is one of the signs that the earlier peoples proposed and then denied. آتينا: verb and agent. ثمود is the first direct object and الناقة the second direct object. مبصرة is a ḥāl. فظلموا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ظلموا is a verb and agent; it contains the sense of "they disbelieved". بها: attached to it. (وَما نُرْسِلُ بِالْآياتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفاً) The wāw is circumstantial, and ما is negative. نرسل: imperfect verb with a latent agent. بالآيات: what was said about this bāʾ has preceded. إلا is a particle of restriction. تخويفا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; you may also make it a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, either from the agent, i.e. "frightening by them", or from the object, i.e. "frightened by them". (وَإِذْ قُلْنا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحاطَ بِالنَّاسِ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "remember". لك: attached to قلنا. إن and its noun; the clause أحاط بالناس is its khabar. (وَما جَعَلْنَا الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْناكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلنَّاسِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative. جعلنا الرؤيا: verb, agent and direct object. He meant by it what he saw after the revelation in his sleep, or on the Night of the Night Journey, there being disagreement; and if it was the Night Journey, then its being named ruʾyā (a dream-vision) is on the grounds that it was at night and because it was imminent and quickly ended, since ruʾyā is for what is judged [Translator's note: the wording is as printed]; as for sight with the eye, it is not called ruʾyā, and for this reason they held against al-Mutanabbī his words:
«ورؤياك أحلى في الجفون من الغمض»
(Seeing you is sweeter to the eyelids than slumber.)
and al-Mutanabbī justifies that he used it for the eyelids because ruʾyā occurs only in them.
التي is an adjective, and أريناك is the ṣila of the relative. إلا is a particle of restriction. فتنة is the second direct object of جعلنا, and للناس is an adjective of فتنة. (وَالشَّجَرَةَ الْمَلْعُونَةَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ) It is conjoined to الرؤيا. الملعونة is an adjective of it, and في القرآن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl. What is meant by it is the tree of zaqqūm, the discussion of which will come in its place in this book; they mocked Muḥammad ﷺ when they heard of the tree of zaqqūm that grows at the bottom of Hell, and said: "He claims that Hell burns stones, and then says that trees grow in it." (وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ فَما يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا طُغْياناً كَبِيراً) The wāw is resumptive. نخوفهم: imperfect verb, latent agent and direct object. فما: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ما is negative. يزيدهم: verb and direct object, the agent being latent, its implied form being "our frightening". إلا is a particle of restriction. طغيانا is the second direct object, and كبيرا an adjective.

dervis-irab:16-21.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُتْرَفِيها): those who live in luxury (munaʿʿimīhā), in the sense of its chiefs. In al-Qāmūs: "al-turfa, with ḍamma, is comfort, good food, and a delicate thing with which you favour your companion; tarifa, like fariḥa, is to live in luxury; atrafathu l-niʿma: comfort made him overbearing, or made him comfortable, like tarrafathu tatrīfan; and al-mutraf, like mukram, is one who is left to do what he wishes and is not prevented, and one living in comfort who is not stopped from his comfort; and tatarrafa is to live in luxury." In Asās al-balāgha: "atrafathu l-niʿma: it made him arrogant; atrafa so-and-so, and he is mutraf; and I seek refuge in Allah from al-itrāf and al-isrāf; and istatrafū: they became insolent and transgressed, and I did not cease being with them in turfa, that is, in comfort."
(مَدْحُوراً): driven away. In al-Qāmūs: "al-daḥr: driving away, removing and repelling, like al-duḥūr; its verb is like jaʿala [i.e. daḥara, yadḥaru], and he is dāḥir and daḥūr."

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا أَرَدْنا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها)
The wāw is resumptive, conveyed to explain the causes by which towns are destroyed and peoples pass away. إذا is an adverb of the future containing the sense of condition, and the clause أردنا is annexed to by the adverb. أن and what is in its scope are an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as the direct object of أردنا, and قرية is a direct object. The clause أمرنا has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of إذا, and مترفيها is an object. ففسقوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and فسقوا is a verb and agent; فيها is attached to فسقوا. (فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْناها تَدْمِيراً)
The fāʾ is a conjunction, and حق is a past verb; عليها is attached to حق and القول is the agent. فدمرناها is a verb, agent and direct object, and تدميرا a mafʿūl muṭlaq. The detail of this eloquent verse will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ) كم is khabariyya (exclamatory), in the position of the accusative as the object of أهلكنا; ومن القرون is in the position of the accusative as the tamyīz of «كم». ومن بعد نوح is attached to an omitted ḥāl or to أهلكنا, in which case من is for beginning. (وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبادِهِ خَبِيراً بَصِيراً) The bāʾ is redundant on the agent, as was recently mentioned. بذنوب عباده is attached to خبيرا بصيرا. (مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنا لَهُ فِيها ما نَشاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ) من is conditional and a mubtadaʾ, and كان is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the clause يريد العاجلة is the khabar of كان. عجلنا is a verb and agent, in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. له is attached to عجلنا, and فيها is attached to an omitted ḥāl. ما is a relative noun and direct object, and the clause نشاء is the ṣila. The preposition and its genitive noun ولمن are a badal of له by repeating the governor, and the clause نريد is the ṣila; the object of نريد is omitted, that is, "for whom We wish to hasten it". The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (ثُمَّ جَعَلْنا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلاها مَذْمُوماً مَدْحُوراً) ثم is a conjunction of delay in time, and جعلنا is a verb and agent. له is in the position of the accusative as the second object of جعلنا, and جهنم the first object of جعلنا. The clause يصلاها is a ḥāl from the pronoun in له, and مذموما is a ḥāl from the pronoun in يصلاها, and likewise مدحورا. (وَمَنْ أَرادَ الْآخِرَةَ وَسَعى لَها سَعْيَها وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ) The wāw is a conjunction and the sentence is conjoined to the preceding one, similar to it in i'rab. وسعى لها is conjoined to أراد, and سعيها is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "the due of its striving". Among the lapses of most commentators, such as Abū l-Baqāʾ, al-Karkhī and others, is that they permitted analysing سعيها as a direct object, forgetting that سعى is an intransitive verb; this is in addition to the fact that its being a maṣdar is perfectly clear. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and هو is a mubtadaʾ and مؤمن a khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in سعى. (فَأُولئِكَ كانَ سَعْيُهُمْ مَشْكُوراً) The fāʾ is the connector of the answer to من, and أولئك is a demonstrative and mubtadaʾ; كان with its noun and khabar, the clause being the khabar of أولئك, and the clause "أولئك كان…" etc. is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هؤُلاءِ وَهَؤُلاءِ مِنْ عَطاءِ رَبِّكَ) كلّا is a fronted direct object of نمد, and the tanwīn is a substitute for annexation, that is, "each one". The agent of نمد is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we", and هؤلاء is a badal of كلّا, and وهؤلاء is conjoined to the first هؤلاء. ومن عطاء ربك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نمد. (وَما كانَ عَطاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial, and ما negative; كان with its noun and khabar.
(انْظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ) انظر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, and كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. فضلنا is a verb and agent, and بعضهم a direct object; وعلى بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضلنا.
(وَلَلْآخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ دَرَجاتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا) The wāw is circumstantial and the lām is the lām of commencement; الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ and أكبر a khabar, and درجات is a tamyīz, accusative with kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. وأكبر is conjoined to the first أكبر, and تفضيلا is a tamyīz.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse, "And when We wish to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they transgress therein, so the word is justified against it and We destroy it utterly", there are various arts:
First: al-iltizām, or "binding oneself to what is not required" (luzūm mā lā yalzam), which has already been discussed at length. It is the binding of one letter or two or more before the rhyme letter (rawī), according to the poet's or writer's capacity, without strain. We restricted it by "without strain" because otherwise it turns into a pale artifice without any trace of beauty, which falls below the degree of eloquence and is not strung on its thread. Here, in His words "mutrafīhā" and "fīhā", the fāʾ is bound before the yāʾ of the ridf, and the yāʾ is kept constant; much of it will come in the Qur'an, and it is among the most elegant of usages. An example in which a sīn is bound before the alif of the ridf is the saying of Abū l-ʿAlāʾ, the author of al-Luzūmiyyāt:
رويدك قد غررت وأنت حر ... بصاحب حيلة يعظ النساء
يحرم فيكم الصهباء صبحا ... ويشربها على عمد مساء
يقول لقد غدوت بلا كساء ... وفي لذاتها رهن الكساء
(Gently: you have been deceived, free man though you are, by a man of tricks who preaches to women. He forbids wine among you in the morning, and drinks it deliberately in the evening. He says, "I have become without a garment", while in its pleasures lies the pledge of the garment.)
Second: the unrestricted trope (majāz mursal) in His saying "We command its affluent ones", because the literal sense of His commanding them to transgress would be that He says to them "Transgress!", and that is false, so it remains that it is figurative. Luxury (al-taraf), which is expansiveness in living and a limitless ease, was made a means to acts of disobedience and to being dragged after desires, as though they were commanded to that, with no escape from it and no release from it; yet there is no command and no commander. It is only wealth, the scout of desire and the courier of heedlessness, which makes ruinous things seem fair to souls, so they give themselves to them and blind themselves to seeing their reality. Their condition may be high and above the usual levels, but it is not long before it plunges, after its guards and protectors have been heedless of it, as happened to the Arabs after their glory had grown vast and their authority wide: they fell from a high place and lost a kingdom they had not preserved like men, in the words of the mother of Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the last of the kings of Banū l-Aḥmar in Andalusia:
ابك مثل النساء ملكا مضاعا ... لم تحافظ عليه مثل الرجال
(Weep like women for a lost kingdom, which you did not guard like men.)
Third: omission (al-ḥadhf). The thing commanded was omitted, and He did not say with what He commanded them, for brevity of speech and in reliance on the listener's immediate understanding, because His saying "so they transgressed therein" indicates it, and this is plentiful speech. You say "I commanded him, and he stood" and "I commanded him, and he read", and nothing is understood from it except that what was commanded was standing and reading; and if you wanted to imply something else, you would strain excessively and omit what has no indication, in a situation where indications for the opposite abound, as we showed you.
Now some have fallen into error, claiming with boundless rashness that amarnā means "We multiplied" (kaththarnā), foremost among those who erred being Abū ʿAlī al-Qālī in his book al-Mumtiʿ, "al-Amālī". He said: "Allah the Exalted said: 'And when We wish to destroy a town, amarnā mutrafīhā', that is, We multiplied." I do not know how this interpretation was permitted for him, because amira is of the pattern fariḥa, with kasra on the mīm, while the reading is amarnā with fatḥa on the mīm, and it is also intransitive, and it is not permissible to interpret it as "he multiplied" with doubled thāʾ unless the mīm is doubled; and it has been read so, so it would have been better for him to point that out. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "'Amarnā' is read short and light, that is, We commanded them to obey; it was also said, We multiplied their blessings, which is the same as the reading with the long vowel (āmarnā); and it is read doubled and short (ammarnā), that is, We made them commanders (umarāʾ); and it was said that it is in the sense of the long one, because it is sometimes made transitive by the hamza and sometimes by doubling."
In His saying "Each We supply, these and these, from the gift of your Lord" there is an ordered lafff and nashr (folding and unfolding): the first "these" refers to the first group, that is, the one who desires this world, and the second "these" to the second group, that is, the one who desires the Hereafter.

* Benefits:
Some asked about the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "See how We have favoured some of them over others", and how disparity among the children of mankind can be right when they are equal. The answer is that the disparity depends on merit and on the measure of what a person gives to his own kind and to society in general. History relates that a group of nobles and those below them gathered at the door of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and permission came out for Bilāl and Ṣuhayb, which was hard on Abū Sufyān. Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said: "We have been undone only by ourselves: they were called and we were called", meaning to Islam, "and they hastened and we were slow. And this is the door of ʿUmar; so how will the disparity be in the Hereafter? If you envy them over the door of ʿUmar, then what Allah has prepared for them in Paradise is greater."

dervis-irab:22-25.t:
* I'rab:
(لا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُوماً مَخْذُولًا): لا is prohibitive; تجعل is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; مع الله is an adverbial attached to an omitted element, being the second object of تجعل; إلها is the first object of تجعل; and آخر is an adjective. فتقعد: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); تقعد is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; مذموما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and مخذولا is a second ḥāl. What is said about تقعد will come later.
(وَقَضى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to explain the status of the parents and the obligation of the children to treat them in a fitting manner. وقضى ربك is a verb and agent; قضى means "He commanded with a decisive command," and it was said, "He enjoined." أن may be a maṣdar particle, in which case لا is negative, تعبدوا is subjunctive by it, and the maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to قضى; it was also said that it is explicative (mufassira), because قضى contains the meaning of "saying" without its letters; or it is the lightened form of the heavy (أنّ), and in both cases لا is prohibitive and تعبدوا is jussive by it, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. إلا is a particle of restriction and إياه is the object. وبالوالدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "and be kind (aḥsinū)"; وإحسانا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) governed by the omitted verb. We attached the two to the omitted verb only because the maṣdar does not have its ṣila (complement) placed before it.
(إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُما أَوْ كِلاهُما): إن is conditional, and ما has been added to it for emphasis; يبلغن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عندك is an adverbial attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; أحدهما is the agent of يبلغن, the mīm and alif being two letters indicating the dual; أو is a conjunction; and كلاهما is conjoined to أحدهما, its sign of nominative being the alif because it is attached to the dual. The meaning of عندك is "while they are in your care, you taking charge of them as they took charge of you in infancy," and in that lies the utmost enjoining of using gentleness and softness of character with them in this state.
(فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ وَلا تَنْهَرْهُما وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً): The fāʾ connects the apodosis; لا is prohibitive; تقل is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; لهما is attached to تقل; أف is a noun of an imperfect verb (ism fiʿl) meaning "to be fed up," and its agent is latent, its implied form being "I," and the clause is the content of what is said; a broad treatment of this word and of the nouns of verbs will come in the section on Benefits. ولا تنهرهما is conjoined to لا تقل لهما, and nahr is rebuking; وقل is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; لهما is attached to قل; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and كريما is an adjective.
(وَاخْفِضْ لَهُما جَناحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ): واخفض لهما is conjoined to وقل لهما; جناح الذل is the direct object; ومن الرحمة is attached to اخفض, so من is causal, that is, "for the sake of mercy," or it marks origin, that is, this lowering arises from the mercy implanted in nature; and you may attach it to an omitted element as a ḥāl.
(وَقُلْ رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُما كَما رَبَّيانِي صَغِيراً): وقل is conjoined to what precedes; رب is the one addressed (vocative), annexed to the first-person yāʾ, with the vocative particle omitted; ارحمهما is a verb of supplication; كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "have mercy on them with a mercy like their rearing of me," or "a mercy like their mercy to me," in which case "rearing" has the meaning of "mercy"; ربياني is a past verb, the alif is the dual pronoun and agent, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the direct object; and صغيرا is a ḥāl from the yāʾ.
(رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِما فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ): ربكم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم is the khabar (predicate); بما is attached to أعلم; and في نفوسكم is the ṣila of ما.
(إِنْ تَكُونُوا صالِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُ كانَ لِلْأَوَّابِينَ غَفُوراً): The clause is a ḥāl clause; إن is conditional; تكونوا is the protasis, and the wāw is its noun; صالحين is its predicate; the fāʾ connects the apodosis; inna and its noun, and the clause كان is its predicate; وللأوابين, that is, "the repentant," is attached to غفورا; and غفورا is the predicate of كان.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the words of Him the Exalted «واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة» there is a metaphor that has occupied the scholars of rhetoric (bayān). We promised you that we would discuss this metaphor at length, so let us examine this subject and cite what the rhetoricians said about it.
It is a makniyya metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya, an implicit metaphor), because ascribing a wing to humility makes the hearer imagine that there is a wing being lowered, while what is meant is "be gentle in your demeanour towards them, and be humble towards them with a humility that sticks you to the dust." The common ground between this metaphor and the reality is that the real wing is on one of the two sides of the bird, and that when the bird lowers its wing — the thing by which it gains strength and rises — it comes down to the ground, falls to the lowest place and sticks to the dust. So the metaphor is makniyya, since gentleness of demeanour is likened to the lowering of the wing, the common ground being tenderness and softness. This is the most beautiful and finest of metaphors, and the speech of the Arabs came upon it.
Al-Ṣūlī mentioned in his book Akhbār Abī Tammām: "They found fault with him, that is, with Abū Tammām, for his saying:
لا تسقني ماء الملام فإنني ... صب قد استعذبت ماء بكائي
(Do not give me to drink the water of reproach, for I am a lover who finds the water of my weeping sweet.)
They said: What is the meaning of 'the water of reproach'? Yet they say: 'a speech with plenty of water' — and how much water there is in the poetry of al-Akhṭal! — this was said by Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb. And they say 'the water of passion' and 'the water of love,' meaning tears. Dhū l-Rumma said:
أأن ترسمت من خرقاء منزلة ... ماء الصبابة من عينيك مسجوم
(Is it that you have traced the abode of Kharqāʾ that the water of passion pours from your eyes?)
and he also said:
أدارا بحزوى هجت للعين عبرة ... فماء الهوى يرفضّ أو يترقرق
(O abode at Ḥazwā, you stirred a tear for the eye; the water of love streams or brims.)
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad — who is a good poet in the view of those who criticize Abū Tammām — said:
أي ماء لماء وجهك يبقى ... بعد ذل الهوى وذل السؤال
(What water will remain for the water of your face after the humiliation of love and the humiliation of begging?)
So he made the face have water. And they said 'the water of youth courses in his cheeks.' So what is wrong if Abū Tammām borrowed a word from all this and put it at the beginning of his verse, when he said at the end of his verse, "for I am a lover who finds the water of my weeping sweet"? He said at its beginning: "Do not give me to drink the water of reproach." The Arabs also carry one word over to another in cases where the meanings are not equal. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: «وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها» — and the second evil is not an evil, because it is a requital, but when He said "the requital of an evil," He said "an evil," carrying it over by the word. Likewise «ومكروا ومكر الله». Likewise «فبشرهم بعذاب أليم»: when He said "give glad tidings to these of the Garden," He said "give glad tidings to those of the punishment," whereas glad tidings (bishāra) occurs only in good, not evil, so the word was carried over by the word. It is said that it was called bishāra only because it spreads the face, whereas evil and dislike contract it. Al-Aʿshā said:
يزيد بغضّ الطرف دوني كأنما ... زوى بين عينيه عليّ المحاجم
(Yazīd lowers his eyes before me, as though cupping glasses had drawn his brows together against me.)
And Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: «واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة». This is the most beautiful and finest of metaphors, and the speech of the Arabs came upon it; so what is wrong if Abū Tammām said: 'Do not give me to drink the water of reproach, for I am a lover who finds the water of my weeping sweet'?"
As for Ibn al-Athīr, he says in his book al-Mathal al-Sāʾir: "His saying was faulted:
لا تسقني ماء الملام فإنني ... صب قد استعذبت ماء بكائي
(Do not give me to drink the water of reproach, for I am a lover who finds the water of my weeping sweet.)
It was said: he gave reproach a water, and that is a remote simile. In my view there is no harm in this simile; it is among the middling similes that are neither praised nor blamed, close in one respect and remote in another. As for the cause of its closeness: reproach is the speech with which the reproached is chided for something he has committed, and that is specific to hearing; Abū Tammām transferred it to the giving of drink, which is specific to the throat, as though he said, 'Do not make me taste reproach.' Had that been possible for him with the metre of the verse, it would have been a good allusion; but he came with the mention of water, which lowered it somewhat. And since hearing gulps down reproach first, just as the throat gulps water, it became as if likened to it; it is a likening of a meaning to a form. As for the cause of the remoteness of this simile: water is pleasant while reproach is disliked, so there is a contrast between them in this respect. So if this simile is remote in one respect, it is close in another, and the one is forgiven for the other; therefore I have made it among the middling similes, neither praised nor blamed.
